original_question: A sequence {Fn } of pairwise disjoint finite subsets of a topological group is called expansive if for every open subset U there is a number m such that Fn ∩ U ̸= ∅ for all n > m. Suppose that a countable group G can be partitioned into countably many dense subsets. Is it true that in G there exists an expansive sequence? Cf. 15.80.
target_in_paper: Problem 21.107 in "New Problems (21st issue, 2026)", which is the countable-group refinement of Problem 15.80.
correct_elements: The draft already matches the paper very closely: it reproduces the paper's definition of an expansive sequence, keeps the pairwise-disjoint finite-set condition, asks exactly the countability-restricted existence question, and even includes the paper's cross-reference to 15.80.
missing_details: G should be stated explicitly to be a countable topological group; otherwise the words "dense" and "open subset" are not anchored to a topology in the question itself.
The partition hypothesis should be made explicit as a disjoint union of countably many dense subsets of G.
The sequence should be explicitly indexed by natural numbers: (F_n)_{n∈N}, with each F_n finite and F_n ∩ F_m = ∅ whenever n ≠ m.
The quantifier "there is a number m" should be specified as "there exists m∈N", i.e. every nonempty open set meets F_n for all sufficiently large n.
To be logically well-formed, "every open subset U" should be read as "every nonempty open subset U"; otherwise U = ∅ would make the definition impossible.
No Hausdorff or other separation assumption is stated in the paper, so a refined version should not add one.
A stand-alone formulation should not rely on the external cross-reference "Cf. 15.80"; that background should be absorbed into the statement while preserving the countable restriction.
refined_question: Let G be a countable topological group, and assume that G can be partitioned into countably many dense subsets. Must there exist a sequence (F_n)_{n∈N} of pairwise disjoint finite subsets of G such that for every nonempty open subset U of G there exists m∈N with F_n ∩ U ≠ ∅ for all n > m?
justification: The nearest official formulation is Problem 21.107, whose wording matches the draft almost verbatim and differs from the earlier Problem 15.80 precisely by adding the hypothesis that G is countable. The paper explicitly cross-references 15.80 from 21.107, and the starred comment under 15.80 records that the unrestricted version is false in general. So the paper's actual intent here is not the broad original question 15.80, but its countable-topological-group refinement 21.107. The rewrite therefore keeps exactly that scope and only makes the ambient topology and quantifiers explicit.
